messages:
ben (Customer): hi team — after rotating our IdP signing cert last night our users started getting 401s when logging into the app. SSO says 'InvalidSignature' in the logs. This started around 01:10 UTC.
alice (Support): sorry you're hitting this, thanks for the heads up. can you share the IdP metadata URL (or paste the metadata) and one full SAMLResponse (redact user specifics) so we can look at the signature cert mismatch? :wave:
ben (Customer): metadata is at https://idp.example-corp.com/metadata.xml and here's the SAML error from our side: "Signature validation failed: no matching certificate found for Signature's KeyInfo". I'll paste the metadata in a bit (can't paste whole SAML resp). We rotated cert B -> C via our IdP last night.
alice (Support): ok grabbing metadata... pinging our metadata fetcher. @metadata-bot fetch https://idp.example-corp.com/metadata.xml
metadata-bot: fetched metadata (size 18.2 KB) from https://idp.example-corp.com/metadata.xml — parsing...
metadata-bot: WARNING: metadata contained two <KeyDescriptor> entries, second one appears incomplete (truncated at boundary). parse error at byte 12479.
ciara (SRE): hmm that looks suspicious. can you try `curl -I` and `curl --raw` against the metadata url? chunked responses sometimes split XML nodes in ways some parsers don't expect.
ben (Customer): output from our side:

$ curl -I https://idp.example-corp.com/metadata.xml
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 01:09:59 GMT
Server: nginx/1.20.1
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Type: application/samlmetadata+xml; charset=utf-8

$ curl --raw https://idp.example-corp.com/metadata.xml | wc -c
12478

ben (Customer): when I fetch raw it's 12478 bytes. if i fetch via browser it looks fine.
alice (Support): that matches our bot's parse boundary. our metadata fetcher expects either Content-Length or a streaming parser that buffers across chunk boundaries — looks like the existing parser trimmed the second KeyDescriptor due to chunk boundary.
ciara (SRE): the symptom you saw (missing cert in the parsed metadata) would cause our verifier to not find the new signing certificate — resulting in InvalidSignature. unusual because chunked should be fine, but some intermediate proxy was re-chunking and splitting inside the <KeyInfo> block. did you have any CDN or WAF in front of the IdP endpoint? @ben (Customer)
ben (Customer): yes we sit behind FastEdge CDN and we recently enabled HTTP/2 + chunked transfer toggle last week. we did not change metadata content.
dmitri (AuthEng): thanks for the details — we've seen a similar edge case before where the metadata fetcher used a simplistic stream read and assumed tag completeness per chunk. I'll triage and push a parser fix today. short-term workaround: upload the IdP metadata file directly in the Redwood Console (Identity -> IdP metadata -> Upload XML) or paste the full metadata into the support upload field. that bypasses the fetcher.
alice (Support): steps for customer to self-remediate (quick):
1) Download metadata to a file: `curl --raw -o idp-metadata.xml https://idp.example-corp.com/metadata.xml`
2) Verify fingerprint of signing certificate in metadata (example commands):

```
# extract cert block from metadata (adjust xpath if needed)
xmllint --xpath 'string(//KeyDescriptor[@use="signing"]/KeyInfo/X509Data/X509Certificate)' idp-metadata.xml > signing.cert.b64
base64 -d signing.cert.b64 > signing.pem
openssl x509 -in signing.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha1
```

3) In Redwood Console go to Settings → SSO → Identity Providers → Upload metadata, choose the file.

If you prefer we can also upload it for you — reply with the file and we'll handle it.
ben (Customer): i can upload; doing steps now. one question: will re-uploading the metadata trigger any downtime? we have users actively logging in.
ciara (SRE): re-uploading metadata is non-disruptive for active sessions — it affects new auth flows. still, suggestion: do it during a low-traffic window if you want extra safety. the console will atomically replace the metadata used for verification.
dmitri (AuthEng): long-term fix: we'll update the metadata fetcher to buffer across chunks and validate xml completeness before passing to the parser. i'll also add a sanity check: if multiple <KeyDescriptor> are found but one looks truncated, we'll retry the fetch a couple times and fall back to full-body download. target is an emergency patch in this sprint.
alice (Support): for our internal runbook/incident notes: root cause = IdP endpoint returned chunked response where a chunk boundary fell inside second <KeyDescriptor>, our metadata fetcher didn't reassemble prior to parse, causing new signing cert to be omitted -> signature mismatch -> login failures. mitigating actions = customer re-uploads metadata OR we add retry/buffer in fetcher.
ben (Customer): uploaded metadata via console at 01:20 UTC. after upload i confirmed new metadata contains cert fingerprint SHA1: 3C:5A:..., and login for a test user is now successful. thanks for the rapid help!
alice (Support): great — can you confirm exactly which cert thumbprint you see in the console so we can close the ticket? also if you can share the CDN config toggle that changed (HTTP/2 chunking) that would help.
ben (Customer): console shows signing cert fingerprint SHA1=3C:5A:9B:4F:22:E1:7A:11:6C:AA:DD:EE:77:88:99:00:11:22:33:44
we toggled 'edge.chunked_rewrite = on' last week per perf experiment.
ciara (SRE): copying action items:
- dmitri to land parser fix and add retry logic (ETA: end of sprint)
- infra to add monitoring alert if metadata parse returns truncated descriptor (owner: ciara)
- support to follow up with customer in 24 hours to confirm no regression (owner: alice)
- customer to report CDN config rollback if they revert for now (owner: ben)

closing notes: ben confirmed fix after metadata upload, marking thread resolved but will track fix in auth backlog. :white_check_mark:
